run.question: Use the custom-crd runbook and check why custom CRD whale-watcher resources are not being reconciled by the operator in namespace app-96

report.summary: The requested runbook could not be used: fetch_skill(skill_id='custom-crd') returned KNOWLEDGE_NOT_FOUND and the only approved runbook for this target is 'service-troubleshooting', so no custom-crd procedure was available to follow. Observed facts for app-96: CRD whalewatchers.ocean.io (group ocean.io, kind WhaleWatcher, Namespaced) is Established and NamesAccepted with a single served/storage version v1, conversion strategy None and no subresources entry (no /status subresource). The only whale/ocean-named workload cluster-wide is Deployment whale-operator in app-96, 1/1 ready, generation 1 revision 1, running python:3.9-slim with /app/operator.py, ServiceAccount whale-operator, code mounted from Secret whale-operator; its pod whale-operator-5f695b7c66-c67gr is Running and Ready with restartCount 0, started 2026-11-22T09:23:06. ClusterRole whale-operator, bound by ClusterRoleBinding whale-operator to that ServiceAccount, grants only get/list/watch on ocean.io whalewatchers — no create/update/patch, no whalewatchers/status, no core events or configmap access. Namespace app-96 and the Deployment were themselves created 2026-11-22T09:23:04, about 39 seconds before the window end. Leading hypothesis (unconfirmed; no error text was obtainable): reconciliation results cannot be persisted because status writes would need update/patch on whalewatchers, which this ClusterRole does not grant. Pod/README-level evidence for a crash, eviction, scheduling failure or config-only restart was checked and rejected. WhaleWatcher object impact itself was not observed: the custom resources could not be listed, the operator code Secret could not be read, the operator produced no usable log view in this Run (log views returned no_data), and Prometheus was unavailable.

claims.text: CRD whalewatchers.ocean.io exists with group ocean.io, kind WhaleWatcher, plural whalewatchers, scope Namespaced, one version v1 that is both served and storage, conversion strategy None, and status conditions Established=True and NamesAccepted=True since 2026-11-22T09:23:04.
CRD version v1 of whalewatchers.ocean.io has subresources = null, so no /status subresource is enabled for this kind.

ClusterRole whale-operator contains exactly one rule: apiGroups [ocean.io], resources [whalewatchers], verbs [get, list, watch]; no create/update/patch verb is present, no whalewatchers/status resource is present, and no rule covers core events or configmaps.

ClusterRoleBinding whale-operator binds ClusterRole whale-operator to ServiceAccount whale-operator in namespace app-96, and that ServiceAccount exists in app-96 with creationTimestamp 2026-11-22T09:23:04.

Deployment whale-operator in app-96 has generation 1 / observedGeneration 1 / revision 1, 1 desired and 1 ready/available replica, conditions Available=True (MinimumReplicasAvailable) and Progressing=True (NewReplicaSetAvailable), and its pod template carries no annotations (no config checksum annotation).

The deployment's only container 'operator' uses image python:3.9-slim with command [python, /app/operator.py], env OPERATOR_NAMESPACE from fieldRef metadata.namespace, serviceAccountName whale-operator, and mounts volume 'operator-code' at /app sourced from the Secret named whale-operator.

Pod whale-operator-5f695b7c66-c67gr is phase Running with container operator ready=true, restartCount 0, state running startedAt 2026-11-22T09:23:06 and empty lastState; pod startTime 2026-11-22T09:23:04; it is owned by ReplicaSet whale-operator-5f695b7c66, which is owned by Deployment whale-operator.

Namespace app-96 was created 2026-11-22T09:23:04 and the in-window events show Deployment whale-operator scaling ReplicaSet whale-operator-5f695b7c66 from 0 to 1 at 09:23:04, the pod Scheduled at 09:23:04 and its container Started at 09:23:06, so the operator had been running only tens of seconds at observation time.

No event in the authorized window references an object of kind WhaleWatcher: the seven in-window events are Deployment/ReplicaSet/Pod startup events in app-96 (ScalingReplicaSet, SuccessfulCreate, Scheduled, Pulled, Created, Started) plus one Warning FailedToCreateEndpoint for Endpoints 'orca' naming namespace app-95, which does not appear in the cluster's namespace list.

The only ConfigMap in app-96 is kube-root-ca.crt (data key ca.crt), and of the 25 deployments cluster-wide the only whale/ocean-named one is whale-operator in app-96 (created 2026-11-22T09:23:04, ready 1).

Leading hypothesis: reconciliation results cannot be written back because ClusterRole whale-operator grants only get/list/watch on ocean.io/whalewatchers and the CRD exposes no whalewatchers/status subresource, so an operator status write via update/patch on whalewatchers would be denied by the API server (403 Forbidden), leaving WhaleWatcher objects unreconciled while the pod stays Running and Ready.

Second candidate: the operator may watch an API group/version or plural that this CRD does not serve (the CRD serves only ocean.io/v1, kind WhaleWatcher, plural whalewatchers), so its informer could fail; this cannot be verified because the operator source is inside Secret whale-operator, which is unreadable.

The premise of sustained non-reconciliation is not directly evidenced: app-96 and Deployment whale-operator were created at 09:23:04 and the container started at 09:23:06, roughly 39 seconds before the query window end, so a genuine reconciliation failure cannot be separated from a freshly started control loop that has not completed informer sync, and no operator output was obtainable in this Run to show either way.

Rejected: the operator pod crashing, being OOMKilled or evicted. The pod is Running and Ready with restartCount 0, its container lastState is empty, and in-window events are only Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started plus SuccessfulCreate and ScalingReplicaSet — no BackOff, Unhealthy, Evicted or OOMKilled.

Rejected: the operator pod was unschedulable or starved for resources. The pod was Scheduled to node opspilot-m1-control-plane, the Deployment reports Available=True, and the container requests 50m CPU / 64Mi memory with limits 100m / 128Mi.

Rejected: a config-only rollout/rescheduling as the trigger. Deployment whale-operator is at generation 1, revision 1 with no pod-template annotations (no checksum), its ReplicaSet was scaled 0->1 at 09:23:04, and the pod has restartCount 0 with no previous container instance, which is initial creation of the workload rather than a restart of an unchanged template.

Grant the verbs needed to persist reconciliation results: add update/patch on ocean.io/whalewatchers (and whalewatchers/status if a status subresource is later enabled) to ClusterRole whale-operator, optionally plus core events create/patch for visibility, then re-observe whether WhaleWatcher status (phase, lastSeen, observationCount) advances.

Make the operator's behaviour observable and confirm its watch target: have it log informer sync results and the Kubernetes API status code on write attempts (no operator output was obtained in this Run), and verify it watches ocean.io/v1 whalewatchers, the only version this CRD serves.

gaps: The requested runbook did not exist: fetch_skill(skill_id='custom-crd') returned INVALID_PARAMS / KNOWLEDGE_NOT_FOUND ('No approved runbook or knowledge entry of this Run's target has this skill_id'), and the tool listed only 'service-troubleshooting' for target m0-otel-20260909, so no custom-crd checklist could be executed.

WhaleWatcher custom resources could not be read: the Kubernetes tools accept only a fixed kind list (no whalewatchers kind), so it is unverified whether any WhaleWatcher objects exist in app-96 and I could not read their status (phase, lastSeen, observationCount) to prove they are unreconciled.

Operator source code could not be inspected: it is mounted from Secret whale-operator, and secrets cannot be read, so the watched group/version/kind, retry and logging behaviour, and whether a status write is even attempted remain unknown.

Operator logs are unknown rather than empty: both fetch_pod_logs queries returned status no_data (views 2370975f-f251-44d3-b110-a7a70f691f6f-t0:862ba8fb-058d-43c9-9b11-c5152c1922a4 and e2d758a0-d64b-46a7-86e6-8012b87ff012-t0:2d66f443-57c2-43bf-be3c-e805fd89657a), and the previous container instance was reported unavailable, so no log line content, error text or 403 response was observed.

Prometheus was unavailable for this Run: get_metric_names, metrics_range_query and execute_prometheus_instant_query all returned status error / SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so kube-state-metrics series such as kube_customresource_* (which could show WhaleWatcher object state), kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total and any reconciliation metric were not checked; these signals are unchecked, not zero.
No failed API call was observed directly: there are no WhaleWatcher-related events and no CR status I could read, so the hypothesised 403 on a status write is unverified.

Absence of namespaced RBAC and of blocking objects cannot be asserted: queries for Roles and RoleBindings in app-96 (view 9d640cc3-8941-453a-bf83-09202f71298f-t1:06c46076-687c-479b-addd-87a05879eb36), NetworkPolicies in app-96 (view 0c1fc878-987d-44aa-94a0-a3206ae36605-t0:37bb3391-47c6-4e75-9fcc-71727ff86ea8) and ValidatingWebhookConfigurations (view 0c1fc878-987d-44aa-94a0-a3206ae36605-t1:070a027b-cc22-4433-8aea-7a3227fa1aac) all returned status no_data, which only shows those queries matched nothing; Services in app-96 returned no_data too (view 675f421e-67b2-47b2-85d6-95d186b8d526-t1:d4061e75-2f63-4b6e-a2f4-b21009e61b59).

The start of the fault is unknown: the evidence context has no change_history integration, and app-96 plus the operator existed only ~39 seconds before the window end, so I cannot say whether reconciliation ever worked.

An object named by an event could not be read: Endpoints 'orca' in namespace app-95 (FailedToCreateEndpoint, 2026-11-22T09:21:00) — namespace app-95 does not appear in the namespace list; it is unrelated to whale-watchers and no impact is claimed from it.

RBAC role bindings that might grant the operator additional rights elsewhere were only checked at cluster scope for whale-named objects; whether any other ClusterRoleBinding or group membership indirectly gives whale-operator write access was not exhaustively verified.
next_steps: Add update/patch verbs (and whalewatchers/status if a status subresource is enabled) to ClusterRole whale-operator and re-check whether WhaleWatcher status fields advance.
Run kubectl get whalewatchers.ocean.io -n app-96 -o yaml to confirm the objects exist and compare status.lastSeen/observationCount against resource age.
Inspect the Secret-mounted /app/operator.py (or enable logging and read kubectl logs for whale-operator-5f695b7c66-c67gr) to capture the exact API error and the watched apiVersion/plural.
Consider enabling subresources.status on the whalewatcher CRD so status can be granted independently of spec edits.
Once Prometheus is reachable, query kube_customresource_* (if kube-state-metrics is configured for this CRD) and container restart metrics for app-96/whale-operator.
